newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Raffles hits high in speculative trade.
newsitem.headline: Raffles hits high in speculative trade.

text.p: Healthcare company Raffles Medical Group hit a new high of Singapore $1.09 in active dealings on Thursday morning trade.
But at 0154 GMT, the share was changing hands at S$1.06, down two cents. Total volume was 1.89 million units.
"The share has been running for the last few days. There is really no reason," said a broker with a Singapore firm.
Dealers said there is speculation in the market Raffles could be taken over by government-owned Pidemco Land, a real estate company.
"The two companies have said they will go into a joint venture to develop a hospital, possibly at Blanco Court which belongs to Pidemco," said a broker.
But analysts said a takeover was not likely as Raffles, 80 percent controlled by founder chairman Loo Choon Yong, was just listed in April.
"There would be a moratorium on Loo selling his shares. And when they start building a hospital, there would probably be a cash call. So I think the price will come off," said one analyst.
